What I checked. Every small model of both critics reproduces (models.py: the tolerance model goes from -0.99999985 to -0.95, the stale-marks model from -30 to -14, the drift model from -1499999 to about -2000, the four bound cases, the crush case, the scaling map, the intransitive comparison). Every worth figure of the worth critic that I recomputed agrees with the files. An exact test of my own (exact.py, rationals, tiny random MIPs with one to three integer and one or two continuous columns, 105,366 models with a bounded or infeasible outcome) applied rule A 29,172 times with a continuous source and 2,895 times with an integer source, rule D 34,110 times and rule E 2,335 times without one changed outcome or optimum; with one condition broken at a time (exact_mut.py) it finds 43 to 811 wrong applications in 6,000 models. It has no tolerances, no crush maps, no stuffing and no conversion.

What changed against the synthesis, and why.
1. Where the rules live. The synthesis had a family exchange_t that scanned every row at its first call and every row with an activity event afterwards, kept four prices per scanned row, and a second family for the conversion that also started from all rows. Both critics showed what that costs (89 of the 240 benchmark instances have integer columns only and can never fire; a price that went stale ended a test for good). Version 2 takes the worth critic's smallest design with three changes: implied equations are a column test inside the dual column family of the nine rules; stuffing is a step of the row visit of the singleton-column family; the single-equation rule and the dominated column share a small family exchange_t that is driven by columns with at most one lock in a direction and is skipped in O(1) when the state has no live continuous column; the conversion (equation test, weak test and scaling together) is driven by a per-row count of live continuous columns that the state keeps.
2. Validity. All eight defects of the validity critic are accepted and repaired: the implied test allows only the rounding of its own candidate; no rule of exchange_t changes a lock or a side and the rule that does (implied equations) runs in another family call; the integrality predicate has the drift guard of row tightening; the type of a column at a record is a notion of the stack; a conversion sets rounded bounds as the start step does and is refused where that would widen a bound; the crush of a conversion reads saved rows; a column scaling scales the offset as well; every fixed case names the counter that must move.
3. Three holes of the same kinds in the nine-rule design and in Stage 1, found while checking the fixes: R6 keeps bound and row with the same tolerance band (my model in models.py loses -0.25 to -0.2); the integrality predicate of R2 and R5 for an integer column has no drift guard; the alias forest's edge test (G/src/alias_forest.cpp:44-57) has none either. The first two are in the list of changes to the nine-rule design; the third is existing code and is named under risks.
4. Worth. The table of dependent instances is rebuilt from the ladder runs. neos-827175 and irish-electricity need none of the five rules; mushroom-best is not an implied-equation instance; implied equations are worth 8 rows on physiciansched3-3 without the conversion, not 209; on the 40 testbed instances the five rules are worth one instance, supportcase42 (140 rows), and ns1208400 where the engine already has HiGHS's size. A further reading that the critics did not have: the 173 rows that the conversion costs on physiciansched3-3 when HiGHS's implied-equation switch is off are explained by that switch also disabling HiGHS's integrality proof for substituting a converted column (G/baseline/HIGHS_DIAG.md:457-460, H/HPresolveImpliedInts.cpp:28-34); in the engine that proof is R2's and R5's own test. That is an inference from the source, not a run.
5. Order. Implied equations; implied integers with the scaling; stuffing; single equation; dominated column; then the gate. Each piece of state and test machinery arrives with the rule that reads it.

One correction for the plan, already made by the synthesis and confirmed here: B/cheap_ablation/off_leftout.csv has the single-equation extension on, so the sentence 'switched off together: 1.0006' (P/DESIGN.md:127-131) describes four of the five rules plus the forcing column.

answers.defect: Validity 1 (serious): the bound counts as implied when the candidate lies within implied_tolerance (about 2e-7, column units); the design keeps that bound and makes the row an equation (rule 2) or fixes k next to it (rule 1)
answers.change: Reproduced (S/models.py V1): the candidate of r1 is 0, the bound 1.5e-7, the old test passes, the equation gives p >= 1.5e-6, G/include/gprs/numerics.hpp:129-132 rounds that to 1, and the optimum goes from -0.99999985 to -0.95. New shared test implied_by_row in src/implied.hpp: the bound is infinite, or the candidate of the lock side (G/src/rules_propagation.cpp:106-132), on an activity that is summed from scratch first when it is not fresh, moved inward by its own candidate_slack (:140-152), still reaches the bound (lower bound: c + s >= bound; upper bound: c - s <= bound). The excess is then at most 2 s, which on a fresh activity is the rounding of the candidate; no share of the feasibility tolerance enters. A bound that make_explicit wrote is a candidate moved outward, so it still passes before and after the switch and in a second presolve (derived, state_and_driver item 5). Rules A and D call it. Fixed tests T1 (the critic's model) and T1b (mine, a locked compensator: S/models2.py, -2.96 to -2.95), wrong engines ie_tol and cf_tol. Decision 2 is reworded. The same band is in R6 of the nine-rule design, see the changes list.

answers.defect: Validity 2 (serious): one scan gives the marks and, from the same scan, rule 2 then rule 5; a row that rule 2 has just turned into an equation goes to rule 5 with marks read before the conversion; a scan asked for inside a walk of rule 1 can apply rule 2
answers.change: Reproduced (models.py V2: -30 to -14 with k fixed at 3). In version 2 the implied equation is a sub-rule of dual_cols_t and the single-equation rule a sub-rule of exchange_t, which runs later in the round, so the two never share a scan. No rule of exchange_t changes a side or a lock (its rules only fix columns, and state_t::fix_col changes no lock count, G/src/state_ops.cpp:278-311); the family asserts that with a counter state_t::lock_changes read at the start and the end of every pass. Marks are computed in the scan that applies the rule. A scan asked for by the dominated-column test computes prices only. The critic's model is fixed test F5; the wrong engine se_mark (lock count tested as >= 1) must fail it.

answers.defect: Validity 3 (serious): the integrality predicate of rule 4 (ratios integral within tol.zero) without the drift guard that row tightening has; the equation test is on in primal-only mode
answers.change: Reproduced (models.py V3: the test passes with |ratio - round| = 5e-10, the drift over y in [0, 2e6] is 1e-3 against 1e-7). One internal function integral_for(row, slot, side) in src/integral.hpp, shared with row tightening: every other free column integer, n_k = round(a_k / a) with |a_k / a - n_k| <= tol.zero, delta_k = |a n_k - a_k|, a column with delta_k != 0 needs two finite bounds, the sum of delta_k * max(|l_k|, |u_k|) plus |a round(side / a) - side| at most coefficient_rounding_share * tol.feasibility (G/src/rules_tightening.cpp:35, 126-145). Used by the equation test, the weak test, the scaling and an integer source of rule A. Fixed test T3 in default and primal-only mode, wrong engine ii_drift. The same predicate without the guard is in R2 and R5 of the nine-rule design (changes list) and in the alias forest (risks).

answers.defect: Validity 4 (serious): the undo of the nine-rule records (merge, col_from_rows) reads input types after a conversion
answers.change: Checked by hand (models2.py: admissible x_j in [3/2, 2], 3/2 with the input type, 2 with the type at the record). postsolve_t gets conversion[col] (the position of the column's implied_integer record in order, or -1) and two readers: integer_at(col, position) = integer in the input, or converted before that position; integer_now(col). Every undo, crush step, push assertion and check clause that depends on a type reads one of them. For a column that its record removes the type at the record is its last type; for the kept column of a merge it is not, which is the critic's second case. Needs towards M1 and M5 are in the changes list. Test: the critic's chain in tests/test_postsolve_records.cpp; wrong engine ii_type (a merge undone with input types).

answers.defect: Validity 5 (minor): after set_col_integer the helper calls tighten_lower / tighten_upper with the present bounds, which do not round a bound within the tolerance inside an integer and can fix at an unrounded bound
answers.change: Reproduced (models.py V5: [0, 0.3/0.1] keeps 2.9999999999999996; [0.2, 0.9999995] is fixed at 0.9999995 by G/src/rules_bounds.cpp:25-26). convert_to_integer now: a finite bound whose rounded value (round_lower_integer / round_upper_integer) would be wider than the stored bound refuses the conversion (a function of the state, statistic ii_refused_bound); otherwise both bounds are set to the rounded values in the three steps of start_step (G/src/presolve.cpp:85-92, shared code), infeasible when they cross by more than the tolerance, fix_column when they meet. The weak modes require exactly integral or infinite bounds, so nothing is rounded there. A scaling snaps a scaled bound to an integer only within 4 rounding units of its size. New invariant in consistency_error: a live integer column has integral bounds (G/src/state_storage.cpp:800-860 has none today). Unit tests with the four cases.

answers.defect: Validity 6 (minor): crush of implied_integer snaps within tol.integrality in column units; a point admitted with a row error of 1e-7 times its largest term is off by more when the coefficient is small
answers.change: Reproduced (models.py V6: x = 6999.9999 is admitted, is 1e-4 from its integer, the floor breaks the row by 0.01). The record names its rows in the saved-row pool: the equation for mode equation, all rows of the column for the weak modes. Replay: mode equation computes v = (b' - saved entries at w) / a and sets w[col] = round(v) when |v - round(v)| * |a| <= tol.feasibility * max(1, largest |term|), else leaves w[col], so a wrong conversion shows as an integrality violation; the weak modes compute the interval [lo, hi] that the saved rows give at w and take max(floor(w), ceil(lo - eps)) for weak_down, min(ceil(w), floor(hi + eps)) for weak_up, eps being the tolerance of the binding row divided by |a|. A row is saved at most once per conversion of its only continuous column, so these saved entries are bounded by one copy of the rows that hold exactly one continuous column. Unit tests of crush with the critic's two rows.

answers.defect: Validity 7 (minor): the structure check composes a col_scale as 'scale times scale, offset unchanged'
answers.change: The reverse pass of compose_records, at a col_scale record, replaces the map s * var + o of the column by (sigma s) * var + sigma o (models.py V7: 1.5, not 3). Because saved rows are composed when the pass reaches their record (D2 Checks B(3)), a record before the scaling reads the column in the old units and a record after it in the new ones without any other rule. Tests: a col_scale followed by a fixing and by an alias with offset, in tests/test_postsolve_records.cpp and test_e2e_check_structure.cpp.

answers.defect: Validity 8 (minor): fixed cases that never reach the rule they are listed for (R5, R6, parallel rows or R2 of the nine rules, or rule 2, take them first)
answers.change: Every fixed case of version 2 names the sub-rule counter that must move (or stay zero) and asserts it, so a case that another rule takes fails. The five cases the critic names are replaced: a source with a second row that does not lock it (F1), a compensator that is no singleton (F9), an equation whose excess two absorbers with finite, not implied bounds cover only together (F6), a weak-test column with two down-locking rows (F3), and the circular pair is kept only as a unit test of the compensator predicate, not as an engine case. I checked T1 and T1b by hand against the text of R2, R5, R6, R7, R8 of D2; the counters are the guard for the rest.

T1 and T1b are inside the oracle class and are run through oracle::check_presolve as well as through their counters; T3 cannot be decided by the oracle (its row tolerance, solve_tolerance times the terms, G/tests/oracle.hpp:34-36 and 59, is of the size of the drift), so it asserts the counters only. answers.defect: Validity, missing: how the entries that tight_row puts into the shared saved-row pool are kept out of the snapshot chain of the nine rules in the structure check
answers.change: A saved row is owned by its record. next_anchor (D2 Checks B(4)) enumerates the saved rows of col_from_rows records only; the rows of tight_row and implied_integer records are never anchors. That is one sentence to honour in M1 (changes list). For an implied_integer record of mode equation the check does more: it recomputes the integrality proof on the saved row with the types at the record's position, and proves the saved row from the next anchor of its row when the two are proportional (counted as untested otherwise).

answers.defect: Validity, missing: 'a row is converted at most once in a presolve' does not hold next to R3
answers.change: The sentence is dropped. R3 (D2 R3) widens an equation to a ranged row, which rule A can convert again. The saved entries of tight_row records are bounded by options_t::saved_row_factor alone; at that limit the conversion is refused and the family reports limited.

answers.defect: Validity, missing: what the structure check does with a comp_fix, a row_exchange target or a merge range when the column was scaled before or after the record
answers.change: With the map rule of validity 7 a comp_fix or fixed_col after a scaling is a constant that the reverse pass multiplies by sigma when it reaches the col_scale, and a merge or saved row before the scaling is composed after the col_scale has been undone. The contract of row_exchange no longer compares targets with original bounds (that would need units per position): fixed entries are followed by fixed_col records, which the bounds test covers through the maps, and absorber targets are used by crush only and tested by crush clause 2.

answers.defect: Validity, missing: the tolerance R >= -tol.cancellation * (...) of rule 1 lets the objective rise by that share times the distance moved, which is not bounded
answers.change: The absolute rise is unbounded, as the critic says. It is bounded relative to the cost terms the exchange moves: at most 1e-12 of |c_k| + sum |p_i a_ik|, times the distance. Clause 4 of the crush check allows identity_tolerance (1e-9) times the sum of |cost * value| of the postsolved and the crushed point (G/check/crush_check.hpp:407-412), and that sum holds the compensators' terms, which are of the size |c_k| * distance when R is near zero; so the allowance is about 1000 times the rise. I keep tol.cancellation because R6 of the nine rules uses the same form for equal costs and because costs that a substitution produced are equal only to rounding. Added: a planted case with a distance of 1e9 (other bound infinite) in the tests of rule D.

answers.defect: Validity, missing (not verified by the critic): PaPILO, HighsPostsolveStack, the event and fixed-point claims of the dual-state items, the worth figures, the scratch test of the dual_state designer

answers.defect: Worth 1 (blocks): a cached price that fails its check at use ends the test of the candidate, and neither the row nor the candidate is taken up again; the fixed-point flag is then true although a second presolve reduces the model
answers.change: The cause in the critic's model is a conversion by rule 2 inside the pass. In version 2 rule A runs in dual_cols_t before exchange_t is called, and exchange_t changes no lock; its only state changes are fixings. Prices are kept for one pass; a fixing of column c clears the cached scan of every row of c (one walk of c, the cost fix_col has anyway), so a cached price is always the price of the state of now and no check at use can fail. The assertion build compares every used price with a fresh scan. The critic's model in both row orders is fixed test F10 and a second-presolve test: after the conversion of row 1 the only raiser of row 0 is j2, R = 3 - 2 = 1, k is fixed at 0 in either order.

answers.defect: Worth 2 (serious): convert_to_integer leaves a bound within the tolerance of an integer that is not one (x in [1e-7, 6])
answers.change: Reproduced (models.py V5: the rounded lower bound 0 is wider than 1e-7). I take the critic's second option: the conversion is refused while a finite bound lies within the feasibility tolerance inside an integer without being equal to it. No bound ever widens (except by the rounding of a scaling's division), so 'explicit bounds only tighten' (G/include/gprs/rules.hpp:140-145) stays true and no row version has to move. See validity 5.

answers.defect: Worth 3 (serious): both families scan every row at their first call and exchange_t scans every row with an activity event afterwards, on every instance; the 3% time rule of L0 cannot be met; four prices per scanned row
answers.change: Recomputed: 18.23 s for the engine on the 240 benchmark instances, 7.10 s in the families, propagation 2.25 s at 6.81 ns per unit, one scan of every row 2.6e8 units; 89 of the 240 have integer columns only and hold 59.8% of the nonzeros and 20.9% of the rows. Version 2: state_t::live_cont_cols makes implied_integer_t and exchange_t inactive in O(1) on those 89; state_t::row_cont_size lets a listed row without exactly one continuous column cost one visit; exchange_t scans a row only when a mark says that a continuous column with at most one lock in a direction points at it; prices exist only for rows scanned in the pass. Rule A adds O(1) per column that R7 visits anyway. Time and work targets are per family and are reports until measured (AM E.6).

answers.defect: Worth 4 (serious): a column that prices rows is listed again by every lock event, and all its rows are rescanned and all their columns retested although no premise changed
answers.change: New column event col_event::few_locks, pushed by the state only when a lock count changed and is now 0 or 1 (change_locks and change_side_locks know the new count, G/src/state_ops.cpp:88-99, 218-232), by set_cost, by move_entry for the target column when a count is at most 1, by set_col_integer and scale_col, and by a bound setter whose new value is infinite. It is a function of the operation. The makespan column of the critic's model (no up lock, m down locks) gets no such event when one of its rows is deleted. Candidates of rule D still need the general lock event (a column becomes fixable when a locking row without a price is deleted), but a candidate costs one walk that ends at its first locking row without a mark. Statistic: rows scanned without a finding.

answers.defect: Worth 5 (serious): the statements that the worth of rules 1 and 5 together is in no stored run, that 1.0006 is a lower bound, and that neos-827175, irish-electricity and most of savsched1 depend on one of the two
answers.change: Recomputed (S/pairs240.py, targets.py, 237 of the 240 benchmark instances). m3_a has the dominated tests, stuffing, implied equations, the conversion and the whole dual-fixing switch off (G/baseline/stage1c_reference_runs.sh:42-56) and equals all cheap rules on neos-827175 (14,039 / 31,598 / 101,260) and irish-electricity (70,646 / 40,633 / 409,523). The single-equation part is bounded by m3_a against off_leftout.csv on its instances: 77 rows, 84 columns, 188 nonzeros on savsched1, kumeu, physiciansched3-3, icir97_tension and huahum. mushroom-best is taken out of the implied-equation list (0 conversions, 48 free column substitutions). Both instances are out of every gate; the targets are those of the worth section.

answers.defect: Worth 6 (serious): implied equations and the conversion are worth their figures only together on three instances; the scaling is built last and a converted column is taken away as a source
answers.change: The figures are right: without the conversion implied equations are worth 8 rows, 5 columns, 21 nonzeros on physiciansched3-3 and nothing on savsched1 and physiciansched6-2; with implied equations off the conversion costs 173 and 24 rows. Accepted: L1's acceptance uses the conversion-off figures; the scaling is built in the milestone of the conversion; an integer column may be the source of rule A when its lock row is integral for it (a switch, on by default). Not accepted as stated: that the 201 rows are carried by converted sources or by the scaling. HiGHS's implied-equation switch also turns off isImpliedIntegral, the proof HiGHS needs to substitute a converted column (G/baseline/HIGHS_DIAG.md:457-460; H/HPresolveImpliedInts.cpp:13-48), and physiciansched3-3 has 194 free column substitutions; so 'conversion on, switch off' leaves converted columns that cannot be substituted. In the engine that proof is the integer case of R2 and R5 (D2 R2), which does not depend on rule A. This is an inference from the source and the counters; L2 measures it and names physiciansched3-3 and savsched1 one by one.

answers.defect: Worth 7 (serious): the milestone order is not the order of worth, and L0 builds state and test machinery long before the rule that reads it
answers.change: Order of version 2: implied equations; implied integers with the scaling; stuffing; single equation; dominated column. L0 holds only the analysis script and the reference runs that wait for the node. The one difference to the critic's order is stuffing before the single equation: stuffing alone reaches seymour1's 32 rows in HiGHS (off_rule5.csv equals all cheap rules there), it is the cheapest of the three to build (a step of an existing row visit), and it brings the record row_exchange and the oracle's group rows that the single-equation rule needs.

answers.defect: Worth 8 (minor): stuffing candidates sorted by cost over coefficient compared by cross-multiplication, which is no strict weak order in floating point
answers.change: Reproduced (models.py W8: 1 and 2 equal, 2 and 3 equal, 1 before 3; 41,224 of 200,000 draws with equal exact ratios). One key per candidate, cost / coefficient rounded once, then the column index; the sort is over that pair, as HiGHS sorts by one quotient (H/HPresolveColStuffing.cpp:34-39).

answers.defect: Worth, missing: a fixed case and a campaign knob for the chain rule 2 then rule 1 against the cost (a covering row x + s >= 1 whose source costs at least as much as x), and what rule 1 loses when implied equations are off or refused
answers.change: Fixed test F9: min x + s1 + s2, rows x + s1 >= 1, x + s2 >= 1, s1 + s2 <= 10 (so that the sources are no singleton columns and R5 does not take them), x binary: rule A makes both covering rows equations, rule D fixes x at 1 with R = -1 + 2 = 1; asserted counters implied_equations 2, dominated_fixings 1. Knob p_cover_source. Stated in rule D: with implied_equations off, or a conversion refused by its side guard or the saved-row limit, rule D loses fixings against the cost, because the covering rows then do not lock x upwards; HiGHS keeps them because its dual bounds do not depend on that switch. The extension that removes the dependence (a compensation with a negative price in a row that does not lock the candidate) is valid by the same exchange and is not built; seymour1 is also reached by stuffing.

answers.defect: Worth, missing: a statement of which forms b1c1s1 needs

rules.name: A. Implied equation (task rule 2). Sub-rule implied_equations of the family dual_cols_t of the nine rules (D2 State and driver 2 and 7; G/src/rules_dual_cols.cpp); milestone L1
rules.condition: Not in primal-only mode; switch options_t::implied_equations. Tested for every column j that the column pass of dual_cols_t visits (the listed live columns and the live columns of the listed rows, each once per call, in index order), after R7's own test of j and only if j is still live. (1) cost_j != 0; d is the direction in which the cost falls (down for cost > 0, up for cost < 0); the lock count of j in direction d (st.down_locks or st.up_locks, G/include/gprs/state.hpp:246-249) is exactly 1. (2) One walk of column j finds the entry (r, a) whose row locks j in d (for d = down: a > 0 with a finite lower side or a < 0 with a finite upper side; for d = up the mirror; G/src/state_ops.cpp:88-99 read backwards); it is the walk R7 makes in that direction. Row r is no equation (row_lower != row_upper). (3) |cost_j| > tol.dual * |a|, HiGHS's strict test of its dual bound cost / coefficient (H/HPresolve.cpp:351-365 with :697-698). (4) S is the side of r that holds the lock, S' = S less the terms of the fixed columns of r, |S'| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility. (5) Type: j is continuous; or j is integer, options_t::integer_sources is on (default on) and integral_for(r, slot of j, S') holds: every other free column of r is integer, the ratios a_k / a and S' / a are integral within tol.zero, and the drift of the rounded ratios over the bounds of those columns is at most coefficient_rounding_share * tol.feasibility. (6) The bound of j in direction d is IEEE infinity, or implied_by_row(r, slot, side S): the candidate of that side for j over the explicit bounds of the other columns (G/src/rules_propagation.cpp:106-132; an activity with an infinite term other than j's own fails; the error guard of :124-128 applies), on an activity that is summed from scratch first if it is not fresh, moved inward by its own candidate_slack (:140-152), reaches the bound. Effect: the free entries of r other than j are saved with a and S' in the saved-row pool of the nine rules, postsolve_t::push_tight_row, then st.set_row_upper(r, row_lower[r]) or st.set_row_lower(r, row_upper[r]), so that both stored sides are the same double. A later column of the same call sees an equation and does nothing. Not taken: a cost of zero or within the dual tolerance; a source with two locks in direction d (HiGHS neither, H/HPresolve.cpp:678-681); an integer source without the proof. Statistics: implied_equations, ie_blocked_bound (finite bound not implied), ie_blocked_type.
rules.validity: Class D, an exchange that moves only column j; off in primal-only mode. Take a feasible point and move x_j in direction d until r is tight at S: x_j' = (S' - sum of the other terms) / a. Row r is the only row that objects to a move in direction d; that is a lock count, an integer. The bound of j in direction d is infinite, or it holds at every point that satisfies r with the other columns inside their explicit bounds, which the moved point does, up to the rounding of the candidate (at most twice its slack; no part of the feasibility tolerance). The bound behind the move is not passed, the cost falls by |cost_j| times the distance. For an integer j the moved value is an integer because the other columns are integers and the ratios and the side are integral in the units of a, with a drift below a tenth of the tolerance in the row. So for every feasible point there is one with r tight and an objective not above; the model with r as an equation relaxes nothing. One implied premise, the lock row itself, recomputed at application. Why 'implied up to rounding' and not the two candidate roundings of the synthesis: the bound stays in the model next to the new equation, and a band of 2e-7 in column units is |a| * 2e-7 in the row, which integer rounding of a neighbour turns into a unit (fixed test T1: -0.99999985 becomes -0.95). Why not HiGHS's strict margin for columns with more than one entry (H/HPresolve.cpp:257-267): HiGHS argues with complementary slackness; the exchange needs only that the bound holds where the lock row holds, and a strict margin would lose every column whose bound was made explicit from its own row. This is HiGHS's rule in lock terms: HiGHS's original row-dual bounds are 0 or infinite (H/HPresolve.cpp:146-149), so its implied bound of r from j is cost / coefficient exactly under (1), (2), (6) (:657-725) and the row becomes an equation when that bound is beyond the dual tolerance (:2647-2664). Wider than HiGHS: an integer source with the proof (HiGHS takes implied-integer columns without re-testing and no true integer, :3629-3631). R5 of the nine rules is this rule followed by R2 for a singleton source whose two ends are implied; R5 runs earlier in the round. Tested in exact arithmetic by S/exact.py: 29,172 applications with a continuous and 2,895 with an integer source on 105,366 tiny models, no changed outcome; with the integrality proof or the implied test removed the same test finds wrong applications. Not run in the engine.
rules.postsolve: New record tight_row {row, col, saved}: saved is an index into the saved-row pool (coefficient a, lower = upper = S', the free entries of r other than j, fixed terms folded in). It removes nothing; the primal postsolve ignores it. Crush, at the record's position of the forward replay: w[col] = (S' - compensated sum of the saved entries at w) / a, rounded to the nearest integer when the column is integer at that position. Crush promises a feasible point of the model after the step with an objective not above; not an equal objective. A wrong implied test shows as a bound violation of the crushed point, a wrong lock count as a violated row, a wrong cost sign or side as a higher objective, a wrong integer source as an integrality violation. Counts in result_t::implied_equations and dual_findings.
rules.cost: O(1) to reject a column that has no cost or not exactly one lock in its cost direction; one walk of the column otherwise (shared with R7); O(1) for the implied test, plus one summation of the row when its activity is not fresh and every other condition holds; the row once for the integrality proof of an integer source. A conversion costs the row once for the saved copy and, when a side turns from infinite to finite, once more for the locks of its columns (G/src/state_ops.cpp:218-232). No row is scanned without a conversion. Saved entries count against options_t::saved_row_factor; at that limit the conversion is refused and the family reports limited. The new equation is listed by row_event::side and reaches the doubleton equations, simple probing and R2 in the next round.

rules.name: B. Implied-integer conversion by the equation test and the weak test (task rule 4). Sub-rules implied_integer_equation and implied_integer_weak of the new family implied_integer_t (rule::implied_integer = 10, G/src/rules_implied_integer.cpp); milestone L2, first step
rules.condition: The family is called only while the state has a live continuous column (state_t::live_cont_cols > 0). It takes its row list (fed by row_event::activity, activity_unread, side and entries; every row at construction). A listed live row r with state_t::row_cont_size[r] != 1 costs one visit. A row with exactly one live continuous column makes that column j a candidate; the row cache names j and holds the bound-independent part of integral_for for the row (not integral; integral with every delta zero; integral with a drift), valid while row_version, csr.size and row_free_size of the row are unchanged; a row whose key changed, or whose class is 'drift', is scanned. Each candidate is tested once per pass, by one walk of its column that reads the cache for every row with row_cont_size == 1. Equation test (also in primal-only mode): some live row i of j is an equation with row_cont_size[i] == 1 and integral_for(i, slot of j, b') holds, b' being the side less the fixed terms under the side guard. A fractional b' / a concludes nothing (HiGHS: H/HPresolveImpliedInts.cpp:112). Weak test (not in primal-only mode), tried when the equation test and the scaling of rule C did not apply: every live row of j has row_cont_size == 1 and is integral for j at each of its finite sides, and each bound of j is infinite or an integer exactly. Bounds: a finite bound of j whose rounded value (round_lower_integer, round_upper_integer) would be wider than the stored bound refuses the conversion (ii_refused_bound). Effect, in the helper convert_to_integer(st, ps, col, mode) next to fix_column: the rows the test used are saved (the equation; for the weak modes every row of j), push_implied_integer(col, mode, rows) with mode equation, weak_down (cost >= 0) or weak_up; st.set_col_integer(col); then both bounds are set to their rounded values in the three steps of the start step (G/src/presolve.cpp:85-92), infeasible when they cross by more than the tolerance, fix_column when they meet. The family serves its list until it stays empty or the budget stops it, so a conversion that leaves another row with one continuous column is followed in the same call.
rules.validity: Equation test: class B, primal; on in primal-only mode. At every feasible point x_j = b'/a - sum of (a_k / a) x_k is an integer minus integers up to a drift below a tenth of the feasibility tolerance in the row, so the type and the inward rounding of the bounds cut no feasible point. Without the drift guard this is false (fixed test T3: x - 1.0000000005 y - w = 0 with y up to 2e6 passes a ratio test of 1e-9 and loses -1499999 for about -2000); the guard is the one row tightening has for the same reason (G/src/rules_tightening.cpp:126-145). Weak test: class D (P/DESIGN.md:477, 670); off in primal-only mode. With the other columns of its rows at integer values every row confines x_j to an interval whose ends are integers or infinite, and so do its bounds; hence floor(x_j) and ceil(x_j) stay inside, and the one in the direction of falling cost does not raise the objective. So an optimal point with x_j integral exists. A column converted earlier is an integer in the model of that moment, so the argument composes along the record order. The reduced model is the original with an integrality condition added: it relaxes nothing. From the conversion on the column is an integer for every rule: its bounds are rounded on every change, its rows can enter row tightening, R7 tightens it, R2 and R5 take it only with their integrality proof, R3 does not take it, rule A takes it as a source only with the proof. HiGHS has both tests (H/HPresolveImpliedInts.cpp:83-142) and also accepts a row that is an equation only by its dual bound (:99-105); here that row is an equation in the state after rule A. HiGHS's clause 'no row is an equation' is not needed: an equation that meets the weak conditions passes the equation test. A conversion never widens a bound, so 'explicit bounds only tighten' stays true. Read and derived; the weak test was confirmed by the validity critic and not rerun by me.
rules.postsolve: New record implied_integer {col, mode, first, count} with its rows in the saved-row pool. It removes nothing. postsolve_t::conversion[col] is set to the record's position; integer_at(col, position) and integer_now(col) read it. postsolve() rounds the reduced value of a column that is integer now, as it rounds integer columns today (G/src/postsolve.cpp:146). Crush, at the record's position: mode equation: v = (b' - saved entries at w) / a; w[col] = round(v) when |v - round(v)| * |a| <= tol.feasibility * max(1, largest |term| of the saved row at w), otherwise w[col] is left, so that a wrong conversion shows as an integrality violation of the crushed point. Weak modes: [lo, hi] is the interval the saved rows give at w; weak_down takes max(floor(w[col]), ceil(lo - eps)), weak_up min(ceil(w[col]), floor(hi + eps)), eps being tol.feasibility * max(1, largest |term|) / |a| of the binding row. The reduced model carries the column as integer; result_t::implied_integer has one flag per reduced column that was continuous in the input (P/DESIGN.md:680). The flag is information for the adapter, not a licence to drop integrality. The weak modes count in dual_findings.
rules.cost: One visit per listed row; one scan per listed row with exactly one continuous column whose key changed or whose class is 'drift'; per candidate a walk of its column with O(1) per row from the cache; a conversion scans the rows it saves and walks the column (set_col_integer). A row belongs to at most one candidate, and it is saved at most once per conversion of its only continuous column, so the saved entries of all conversions are bounded by one copy of the rows that hold exactly one continuous column; they count against saved_row_factor and the family reports limited at that limit. Budget {4, 2, 100000}, last phase of the round. Memory: 13 bytes per row for the cache, allocated at the first call.

rules.name: C. Column scaling for the conversion (part of task rule 4; HiGHS's transform x = s z). Sub-rule implied_integer_scaling of implied_integer_t; milestone L2, second step
rules.condition: For a candidate j of rule B and a live equation r with row_cont_size[r] == 1 on which the equation test failed on a ratio or on the side (not on the drift guard). The other free coefficients and b' have a common integral scale m <= max_integral_scale = 1000, found with integral_denominator (G/src/rules_tightening.cpp:55-72, moved to src/integral.hpp without change). sigma = 1 / (|a_j| m) is not 1 and lies in [1/1024, 1024] (col_scale_limit); with sigma == 1 the equation test passes without a scaling. integral_for holds for the row with the coefficient of j replaced by sign(a_j) / m (a dry run on the numbers the row will have). The scaled cost and every scaled coefficient of j are finite, not zero and at most max_integral_coefficient (1e12). Scaled bounds: a finite bound b / sigma within 4 rounding units of its size of an integer becomes that integer; any other finite scaled bound must not be widened by the integer rounding of rule B, else the scaling is refused. Effect, one transaction: push_col_scale(j, sigma); st.scale_col(j, sigma, the two new bounds); convert_to_integer(j, equation) with r as its row. HiGHS scales whenever its scale is not 1 (H/HPresolve.cpp:2842-2857); here the equation test goes first, so a column keeps its units where integrality can be had without a scaling.
rules.validity: Class S and B, primal; on in primal-only mode. x_j = sigma z with sigma > 0 is an exact change of variable; in the equation the coefficient of z is +1/m or -1/m and every other coefficient and the side are integral multiples of 1/m, so z is integral at every feasible point by the proof of rule B. This is H/HPresolve.cpp:2817-2858 (read). Floating point: each coefficient, the cost and each bound of j is rounded once; a bound that the division leaves one rounding step inside an integer (0.3 / 0.1 = 2.9999999999999996) is snapped, which is the rounding of that division and no relaxation by a tolerance; lock counts do not change because sigma is positive. state_t::scale_col moves row_version of the rows of j and clears the recorded implied bounds of j, as an entry change does.
rules.postsolve: New record col_scale {col, scale}. The column keeps its index with a new meaning; records pushed later are in units of z. Undo, at the record's place in the reverse order: x[col] = scale * x[col]. Crush: w[col] = w[col] / scale. The structure check's reverse pass replaces the column's map s * var + o by (scale s) * var + scale o. The adapter's column map gets the 'transformed' marker of P/DESIGN.md:680.
rules.cost: One scan of the equation for the scale (the scan of rule B's candidate test), then the entries of column j twice (scale_col and set_col_integer) and the saved copy of the equation.

rules.name: S. Column stuffing (task rule 3, HiGHS rule bit 19). Sub-rule column_stuffing of the family singleton_cols_t of the nine rules, a step of its row visit; milestone L3
rules.condition: Not in primal-only mode. In the visit of a row r by singleton_cols_t (D2 State and driver 7: a listed row, or the row of a listed singleton column), after R5 found no column to remove, when r has exactly one finite side and at least two free entries. The row is read as sum a' x <= U' (a' = a for a finite upper side, -a for a finite lower side; U' the side less the fixed terms with the sign adjusted; side guard). Candidates are the live singleton columns t of r whose cost pushes against the row: a'_t > 0 with cost_t < 0, or a'_t < 0 with cost_t > 0. Either all candidates are integer with equal |a|, or the integer ones are dropped and the continuous ones remain (H/HPresolveColStuffing.cpp:139-170). At least two candidates: with one, the two tests are the redundant row and the forcing row of the row rules. Each candidate has the bound rho of its smallest term, which must be finite, the bound kappa that its cost prefers, and delta_t = |a_t| (u_t - l_t). Every other column counts with its full range (a singleton column whose cost does not push against the row has no lock in its cost direction and was fixed by the lock rule earlier in the round). As compensated sums from one scan: Amin0 = the smallest activity of the row and Amax0 = the largest activity less the sum of the deltas (candidates at rho); an infinite term in one of them switches off the test that reads it. Sort key per candidate: cost_t / a'_t, one division rounded once, then the column index; the sort is over that pair. In that order, with Umax = Amax0 and Lmin = Amin0: the loop ends at the first candidate whose kappa is infinite; (1) if Umax + delta_t - U' <= error + forcing_rounding_units * rounding_unit * size (the allowance of a forcing row with a continuous column, G/src/rules_rows.cpp:38, 179), t gets the role fix_kappa; (2) else if Lmin - U' is at least the error bound of the sum, t gets the role fix_rho; else keep; then Umax and Lmin both grow by delta_t (H/HPresolveColStuffing.cpp:193-224). Effect: one row_exchange record (mode stuffing, all candidates in sorted order with their role), then fix_column for every fixed candidate whose value passes the size guard |v| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility; a candidate that fails it is recorded as keep. No cap on the row length (HiGHS's 1000, :237-239, is not needed for the cost; option stuffing_row_limit, default 0).
rules.validity: Class D, exchanges inside one row; off in primal-only mode. The candidates are in no other row, so for given values of the other columns the row is a one-row knapsack over the candidates and capacity goes to them in the order of cost per unit (Gamrath et al. 2015, cited at H/HPresolveColStuffing.cpp:17-18). Write g_p in [0, delta_p] for the activity of candidate p above rho. Test (1): raise g_t to delta_t; if the row is then violated, lower candidates behind t; with all of them at zero the activity is at most Umax + delta_t <= U', the other columns being counted at their largest terms and the candidates before t as full; a unit lowered costs no more than a unit raised gains, because the keys are sorted. Test (2), at its first firing for candidate t, with F1 the earlier candidates fixed at kappa and N the earlier ones that stay free: every feasible point has the activity of F1, N, t and the later candidates above rho at most U' - Amin0, and the condition says Amin0 plus the deltas of F1 and N is at least U', so the room in N is at least g_t plus all later g; move g_t into N: the activity does not change and the objective does not rise. The same inequality fires the test for every later candidate. Integer candidates have equal weights, so every move is a whole number of units between integral bounds. Differences to HiGHS: both tests allow 1e-6 there (:204-209), here only rounding, so that the reduced model never needs the tolerance to stay feasible; test (2) is the condition the exchange proves, HiGHS asks for delta_t more to get a non-degenerate basis (:210-219), so ours fixes at least what HiGHS fixes. Two keys that differ by the rounding of one division can be sorted either way by the index; the objective then rises by at most that rounding of the moved cost. Derived by the designers; the validity critic confirmed both tests by reading; not rerun by me and not run in the engine.
rules.postsolve: Record row_exchange {row, mode, first, count} with pooled entries {col, coefficient, bound_from, bound_to, role}; for mode stuffing the entries are the candidates in sorted order with normalised coefficient, rho, kappa and role fix_kappa, fix_rho or keep. It removes no column; the fixed_col records of the fixed candidates follow it. The primal postsolve ignores it. Crush, entry by entry in recorded order: fix_kappa raises the column to kappa and then lowers later entries, from the end of the list backwards, by the same activity in total or until all are at rho; fix_rho lowers the column to rho and raises earlier entries of role keep, from the start, by the same activity (they have the room where the rule is right). No row activity is read, so no saved row. The result is feasible with an objective not above; a wrong firing shows as a violated row or a higher objective of the crushed point. The exchange code is one function shared by crush and its unit tests. Counts in result_t::stuffing_fixings and dual_findings.
rules.cost: Nothing for a visited row with fewer than two candidates (the visit has its singleton columns already). With two or more: the sums from one scan of the row, a sort of the candidates (charged n log n), O(1) per candidate. Pool: one entry per candidate per application, counted against saved_row_factor.

rules.name: E. Single-equation extension of dual fixing (task rule 5, inside HiGHS rule bit 17). Sub-rule single_equation of the new family exchange_t (rule::exchange = 11, G/src/rules_exchange.cpp); milestone L4
rules.condition: Not in primal-only mode; the family is called only while the state has a live continuous column. Row E is live with row_lower == row_upper == b finite and is scanned by the family in this pass: it carries the family's mark has_source (a continuous column with at most one lock in a direction pointed at it when that column was last processed) and it is the lock row of a column listed by col_event::few_locks or is on the family's row list. b' = b less the terms of the fixed columns, |b'| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility. The scan gives every free entry (k, a) a mark from the lock counts and the cost of now. Mark +1 (its term can fall without cost and without another lock): for a > 0, cost_k >= 0 and st.down_locks[k] == 1; for a < 0, cost_k <= 0 and st.up_locks[k] == 1; the one lock is E, which locks both ways. Otherwise mark -1 (its term can rise): for a > 0, cost_k <= 0 and up_locks == 1; for a < 0, cost_k >= 0 and down_locks == 1. Otherwise 0. This is checkColumn of H/HPresolveDualFixing.cpp:110-131 with the lock counts in place of its scan of the column, +1 tried first as at :167-177. Case 1: F = the columns with mark -1 whose target (the bound of their largest term) passes the size guard |v| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility, K = the continuous columns with mark +1; both not empty. Sum1 = sum over the entries outside K of the largest value of a x_k plus sum over K of the smallest value, summed from scratch with dd_add_product in the same scan; every bound it needs is finite and no term counts as infinite. It fires when Sum1 - b' <= error + forcing_rounding_units * rounding_unit * size (G/src/rules_rows.cpp:38, 179). Effect: push_row_exchange (mode single_equation: the columns of F with coefficient and target as role fixed, the columns of K in index order with coefficient and the bound of their smallest term as role absorber), then fix_column for every column of F. Case 2, tried when case 1 did not fire, is the mirror (F' = mark +1, K' = continuous mark -1, Sum2 = smallest over the entries outside K' plus largest over K', fires when b' - Sum2 is within the same allowance, F' fixed at the bounds of the smallest terms). With K (K') empty the claim is the forcing or infeasible row of the row rules and is left to them. Nothing changes the state between the marks and the fixings; the family asserts that state_t::lock_changes did not move during the pass.
rules.validity: Class D, an exchange inside one equation; off in primal-only mode. Case 1 with all coefficients taken positive: move every column of F to its upper bound; the activity of E rises by Delta >= 0. Lower the terms of the columns of K by Delta in all. They have the room: b' is the activity at the point, so the room of K less Delta is at least b' - Sum1 >= 0. K is continuous, so the amount can be taken exactly. Every column of F moves in a direction in which only E locks it and its cost does not rise; the same for K; a row that holds one of them does not lock it in its direction. Integer columns of F land on integral bounds; an integer column with mark +1 is no absorber and is counted at its largest term (HiGHS the same, H/HPresolveDualFixing.cpp:193-211; HiGHS's absorbers are columns of type continuous, so a converted column is none there either). Dropping a column from F by the size guard leaves it at its largest term in Sum1, which is where F is counted, so a subset is valid. This is section 6.1 of Achterberg et al. as HiGHS implements it (:158-229, read). Differences: HiGHS accepts Sum1 <= b + 1e-6 (:219-220), here only what rounding explains; HiGHS skips rows that are redundant over implied bounds when it decides the marks (:117), here the cascade has deleted redundant rows before the family runs. The marks must be those of the state at application: with marks read before another rule turned a second row of k into an equation the rule loses an optimum (fixed test F5, -30 to -14); here the rule that changes sides runs in another family call and no rule of this family changes a lock. Tested in exact arithmetic (S/exact.py: 1,459 applications of case 1 and 876 of case 2, no changed outcome). Not run in the engine.
rules.postsolve: Record row_exchange with mode single_equation (the kind of rule S): entries {col, coefficient, bound_from, bound_to, role}, roles fixed and absorber; bound_to is the value a fixed column gets or the bound an absorber may move to. It removes no column; the fixed_col records of exactly its fixed entries follow it. The primal postsolve ignores it. Crush, at the record's position: Delta = compensated sum over the fixed entries of coefficient * (bound_to - w[col]); every fixed entry is set to its target; then the absorbers, in recorded order, each move towards their bound by as much as cancels what is left of Delta. No saved row is needed, because the equation holds at the point before the move. A rest of Delta that the absorbers cannot take shows as a violation of E, which is how a wrong firing is seen. Counts in result_t::single_equation_fixings and dual_findings.
rules.cost: A row is scanned only when it carries the mark and was listed or pointed at in this pass; the marks and both sums come from that one scan, O(1) per entry, with no scan of a column (HiGHS scans every column of the row twice and reruns behind a flag, H/HPresolveDualFixing.cpp:112-129, 300-315). Finding the lock row of a listed column with a single lock is one walk of that column up to the locking entry; for an integer column the walk is made only while a marked row exists. A firing costs the entries of the fixed columns. Pool: the fixed columns and the absorbers once per application, counted against saved_row_factor. Budget of the family {8, 4, 100000}.

rules.name: D. Dominated and weakly dominated column by the bound on the reduced cost, as a fixing with compensators (task rule 1; HiGHS rule bits 5 and 23 beyond the forcing column). Sub-rule dominated_columns of exchange_t; milestone L5
rules.condition: Not in primal-only mode. Definitions on the state of now. A live continuous column j with entry a_ij is a compensator of row i in row direction s (raise or lower the activity), moving in column direction d (up when s is raise and a_ij > 0 or s is lower and a_ij < 0, else down), when: (C1) the lock count of j in direction d, less 1 if row i locks j in d, is 0; (C2) the bound of j in direction d is IEEE infinity, or row i locks j in d and implied_by_row(i, slot, that side) holds (the test of rule A, rounding only). Its price is p = (cost_j for d = up, -cost_j for d = down) / |a_ij|, admissible when finite and |p| <= price_limit = 1e7 (HiGHS's limit, H/HPresolve.cpp:700-702). It is 'free' without a lock from i and 'locked' with one. A scan of a row gives, for raise and for lower, the two compensators with the smallest price, ties to the smaller column index. Candidates: the columns listed by the general lock and cost event (col_list::exchange) and the free columns of the rows scanned in this pass that have a price, each once per pass, in index order, of any type. For candidate k both directions are tried, down first when cost_k >= 0, else up first. Direction D has the target v = col_lower[k] (down) or col_upper[k] (up). (1) v is finite, |v| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility, and no term a v of the column counts as infinite. (2) The lock count of k in direction D is at least 1; with 0 the lock rule owns the column (G/src/rules_dual_fixing.cpp:39-41). (3) One walk over the live entries (i, a) of k. An entry whose row does not lock k in D adds nothing. For an entry whose row locks k in D the row must carry the mark has_source (else the test ends) and gives its best price in the row direction that undoes the move of k (raise when D is down and a > 0 or D is up and a < 0, else lower), the second best when the best is k itself; the price comes from the scan of this pass, made on demand if the row was not scanned (such a scan computes prices only and applies no rule); |a / a_ij| <= comp_ratio_limit = 1000. A locking row without a price ends the test. (4) The rate R = s cost_k - sum over the locking rows of price_i |a|, s = +1 for down and -1 for up, as a compensated sum. The column is fixed when R >= -tol.cancellation * (|cost_k| + sum of |price_i a|). Effect: fix_column_compensated(st, ps, k, v, terms), which pushes the record and calls st.fix_col; the terms are {j_i, a_ik / a_ij}; then the cached scans of all rows of k are cleared. The family counts the fixings by the number of locked compensators with a finite bound (0, 1, 2 or more) and the candidates that fail only on an infinite target with R > 0 (dominated_unbounded). Not taken: 'unbounded or infeasible' from a strictly dominated column with an infinite target (HiGHS returns it, H/HPresolve.cpp:3662-3663); an integer compensator; a compensation with a negative price in a row that does not lock k (so a fixing against the cost needs rule A to have made such rows equations first).
rules.validity: Class D, an exchange with a recorded compensation; off in primal-only mode. From a feasible point move x_k to v, a change of delta in direction D, and move every compensator j_i by |a_ik / a_ij| delta in its direction. (i) A row that does not lock k in D only gains from the move of k. (ii) A locking row i with a free compensator has one finite side; the compensator restores what k took; any compensator of another row that has an entry in i has no lock from i in its direction and so moves the activity away from the finite side. (iii) A locking row i with a locked compensator has two finite sides (the compensator's move pushes towards the side opposite to the one that locks k); the compensator of another row cannot have an entry in i, because a row with two finite sides locks each of its columns both ways and C1 would fail for it; so the only moving columns of i are k and its own compensator, whose moves cancel. (iv) Any other row that holds a compensator does not lock it in its direction (C1). (v) A free compensator has an infinite bound in its direction. A locked one has a bound that is infinite or implied by its row i up to rounding; after the exchange row i holds and every other column of it is inside its explicit bounds, so the compensator is inside its bound up to that rounding. Each implied premise is used only in its own row, where nothing else moved, so the premises cannot lean on each other; the circular pair x - y <= 0, y - x <= 0 gives no compensator, because neither column passes C1. (vi) The objective changes by -delta R, not positive up to tol.cancellation of the moved cost terms; that tolerance is the one R6 of the nine rules uses for equal costs, and it is far inside clause 4 of the crush check, which allows 1e-9 of the sum of |cost * value| of the points (G/check/crush_check.hpp:407-412). An integer k lands on an integral bound; compensators are continuous. The reduced model is the original with a bound tightened. This is HiGHS's test cost_k - sup sum a_ik y_i >= 0 over the tighter of original and implied dual bounds (H/HPresolve.cpp:3636-3700) with each bound read as a price; with only original bounds it is the lock rule. Narrower than HiGHS: continuous compensators only (HiGHS also takes implied-integer columns, :3629-3631); no status from an infinite target; a fixing against the cost only through rows that are equations. Why the tolerance of C2 is rounding only: with two candidate roundings a locked compensator may pass its bound by 2e-7, and its equation turns that into a unit of an integer neighbour (fixed test T1b, my model, S/models2.py: -2.96 becomes -2.95). The plan's guard 'at most one implied premise per derivation' (P/DESIGN.md:489) is not kept to the letter: there is one per locking row with a locked compensator (decision 3). Tested in exact arithmetic (S/exact.py: 34,110 applications, 27,331 on integer and 6,779 on continuous columns, no changed outcome; with C1 or C2 broken the test finds hundreds of wrong applications). Not run in the engine.
rules.postsolve: New record comp_fix {col, value, first, count} with pooled terms {col, factor}; it removes col, as a fixed_col record does. With one term it has the content of parallel_fix of the nine rules; it is a kind of its own so that M3 needs no change. Undo: x[col] = value. Crush, at the record's position: delta = w[col] - value; w[t.col] += t.factor * delta for every term; col is dropped. Stack contract: the value is finite, and integral for a column that is integer at the record's position; every term names another column that no earlier record removed and that is continuous at the record's position, with a finite factor other than zero. Crush promises a feasible point with an objective not above. Counts in result_t::dominated_fixings and dual_findings.
rules.cost: A listed column costs O(1) on its target and lock count, then one walk that ends at the first locking row without the mark. A row is scanned for its prices at most once per pass and once more after each fixing of one of its columns. Rows are scanned only where a continuous column with at most one lock in a direction points at them; on an instance without such a column the family does nothing after its lists are taken. A firing adds the entries of k (fix_col and the clearing of its rows' scans). Pool: one term per locking row of a fixed column, counted against saved_row_factor. Memory: 64 bytes per row scanned in the pass.
